chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Abi Najran, from al-Muthanna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said:

I asked al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) about the ring of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) — to whom did it go? And I mentioned to him that I had heard that it was looted from his finger among what was looted.

He (peace be upon him) said: It is not as they say. Indeed, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) bequeathed to his son Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and placed his ring on his finger, and delegated his command to him, just as the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) had done with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the Commander of the Faithful had done with al-Hasan (peace be upon them both), and al-Hasan had done with al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). Then that ring came to my father (peace be upon him) after his father, and from him it came to me. So it is with me, and I wear it every Friday and pray with it.

Muhammad ibn Muslim said: So I entered upon him on Friday and he was praying. When he finished the prayer, he extended his hand toward me, and I saw on his finger a ring whose inscription was: "There is no god but God, a preparation for the meeting with God." Then he said: "This is the ring of my grandfather Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali, peace be upon them."

key_terms.أوصى: Bequeathed — used in Shia theology for the formal transfer of Imamate
key_terms.خاتم: Ring/signet ring — a physical symbol of the transfer of Imamate authority
key_terms.فوض: Delegated/entrusted — signifying the transfer of divine authority

ai.seo_question: What happened to the ring of Imam Husayn after Karbala?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the widespread belief that Imam Husayn's ring was looted at Karbala, explaining that it was formally bequeathed to Imam Zayn al-Abidin as part of a succession tradition established by the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW). The ring, inscribed 'There is no god but God, preparation for the meeting with God,' was passed through each Imam as a symbol of authority. The narrator Muhammad ibn Muslim personally witnessed Imam al-Sadiq wearing it during Friday prayer.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abu’l Khattab from Ibn Abi Najran from al-Muthanna from Muhammad b. Muslim.  He said:

I asked al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) about the ring of al-Husayn b. `Ali (as) – to whom did it go? And I mentioned to him that I had heard that it was looted from his finger along with what was looted.

He (as) said: It is not as they say. Surely, al-Husayn (as) bequeathed to his son `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) and put his ring on his finger and delegated to him his command like the Messenger of Allah (s) had done with Amir al-Mu’minin (as) and Amir al-Mu’minin had done with al-Hasan (as) and al-Hasan had done with al-Husayn (as). Then that ring came to my father (as) after his father and from him it came to me. So, it is with me and I wear it every Friday and I pray with it.

Muhammad b. Muslim said: So, I entered upon him on Friday and he was praying. When he had finished the salah he extended his hand towards me. And I saw on his finger a ring; its inscription was “There is no god but Allah, prepare for the meeting with Allah.” (La ilaha illa ‘llah, `uddatu liliqaa’illah) – then he said: This is the ring of my grandfather Abu `Abdillah al-Husayn b. `Ali (as).
